label: Point-of-Care Against Comprehensive Ultrasound (Lecture 20)
rows: Bedside, REAL-TIME answers to a diagnostic question; FOCUSED, limited, goal directed; INTERPRETED BY THE PROVIDER PERFORMING IT.
Ordered AFTER evaluating the patient; comprehensive but takes HOURS TO DAYS; performed by a certified SONOGRAPHER, read by a RADIOLOGIST.
An extension of the history and physical exam (often when the patient can't give enough information); a complement to the workup; formal imaging may often still follow.
Likely deep vein thrombosis, stable: "needs formal US [ultrasound], probably not POCUS [point-of-care ultrasound]."

label: Indications, Contraindications, Procedures
rows: Trauma, cardiac, pulmonary, vasculature, ophthalmic, renal, gallbladder, appendix, scrotal, obstetric/gynecologic.
GLOBE RUPTURE; must NOT DELAY LIFESAVING MEASURES; some locations not amenable to ultrasound.
Central venous catheter insertion, paracentesis, thoracentesis; vascular: central lines, ultrasound-guided intravenous lines, deep vein thrombosis.
Artery: pulsatile, minimal compressibility. Vein: COMPLETELY compressible (unless filled with clot).

label: The Machine, the Probe and Orientation
rows: Sound above human hearing (more than 20,000 hertz); piezoelectric crystals in the probe send the wave and read the echo.
HIGHER = better RESOLUTION, less depth. LOWER = better DEPTH, less resolution. Short wavelength = high frequency.
Depth = how far you are zoomed in. Gain = brightness.
Fan, rock, sweep, slide, rotate, compress.
Phased array (cardiac), linear (pneumothorax), curvilinear (effusion, edema, pneumonia), endocavitary.
Probe/orientation marker: point it to YOUR LEFT (the patient's right); CARDIOLOGY PUTS IT OPPOSITE; match the screen marker.
Transverse (axial: indicator to your left, look through the patient) · sagittal (longitudinal) · coronal (frontal).

label: Echogenicity
rows: BLACK · echoes nothing back · fluid-filled structures
GRAY · less echo than surroundings · liver, spleen
WHITE · dense, more echoes · bone, stones

mnemonic.hook: Read the prefix as the amount of echo coming back.

label: Artifacts
rows: Behind HYPERECHOIC structures (ribs, stones): a dark band. Air shadows look "dirtier" than bone.
Behind FLUID-filled structures: the area deep to it looks BRIGHT (can obscure it).
REFRACTION: sound "bends" off the edge of a fluid-filled structure.
REVERBERATION off a strong reflector (the diaphragm): the liver mirrored above it. Normal.
A strong reflector OUTSIDE the central beam appears inside it (echoes in the gallbladder).
★ A lines · comet tails · B lines
Reverberations. A lines: horizontal, NORMAL lung. Comet tails: vertical off calcifications, cholesterol, metal. B lines: vertical in the LUNG, air-water interface = PULMONARY EDEMA.

label: Modes and Color Doppler
rows: Brightness: the standard two-dimensional gray-scale image.
Motion: ONE LINE of the B-mode image over time. Common uses: FETAL ultrasound and PNEUMOTHORAX.
M-mode over the chest: "ocean" above the pleural line + "sand on the beach" below = NO pneumothorax; lines all the way down (barcode) = PNEUMOTHORAX.
Direction and velocity by color. BART: Blue Away, Red Towards; perpendicular = black. Blue/red do NOT mean vein/artery. Artifacts: twinkle, aliasing.

label: The Four Cardiac Windows
rows: Beside the sternum, heart lengthwise · OFTEN THE EASIEST view
Rotate 90 degrees, marker to the patient's RIGHT HIP · cross-section of the ventricles; MITRAL and AORTIC VALVES
Under the xiphoid, just right of midline, LIVER as the window · BEST for PERICARDIAL EFFUSION (most are inferior)
From the apex; sometimes difficult · ALL FOUR chambers; RIGHT VENTRICULAR DILATION/STRAIN; rotate for the 5-chamber view (aortic valve/outflow tract)

mnemonic.hook: Each window's one job, in the order it is taught.
mnemonic.breaks: The probe for all four is the phased array; this aid covers the job, not the probe position.

label: Pulmonary Assessment
rows: LINEAR for pneumothorax; CURVILINEAR for effusion, edema, pneumonia. Anterior and posterior views; BLUE protocol (bilateral lung ultrasound in emergency).
A lines, lung sliding, the seashore.
Dark fluid above the diaphragm; ABSENCE OF MIRRORING; the SPINE SIGN (fluid carries the sound, vertebrae seen).
Bronchograms; B lines; HEPATIZATION (lung looks like liver); effusion or empyema; spine sign.
Barcode in M-mode; LUNG POINT rules it in (BLUE tree: sliding abolished, A'-profile + lung point).

label: Abdominal Assessment
rows: Gallbladder, inferior vena cava, aorta, many others.
STONE (posterior acoustic shadow) + WALL THICKENING + PERICHOLECYSTIC FLUID + SONOGRAPHIC MURPHY SIGN.
Volume status and fluid responsiveness. COLLAPSE MORE THAN 50% WITH INSPIRATION = dehydration or fluid responsiveness. Probe longitudinal, just RIGHT of midline.
Arteries pulsatile, minimally compressible; the vena cava and aorta side by side over the vertebral body shadow.

label: Protocols and the EFAST Windows
rows: FAST/EFAST (focused assessment with sonography in trauma; extended)
RUSH (rapid ultrasound in shock and hypotension)
Peritoneal AND pleural free fluid (a dark stripe in Morison's pouch, fluid at the spleen)

label: Soft Tissue and the Veins
rows: Anechoic/hypoechoic COLLECTION (varies a lot); PUS SHIFTS WITH COMPRESSING.
Compress: THROMBUS WILL NOT COMPRESS (major diagnostic feature). Content hypo- or hyperechoic with CHRONICITY. May LOSE COLOR FLOW.

label: Putting It Together
rows: Sudden respiratory distress: a bedside answer now. Very high blood pressure + crackles + diffuse B lines = FLASH PULMONARY EDEMA.
Likely deep vein thrombosis with normal vital signs: formal ultrasound, probably not point-of-care.
Scan + history + exam + vital signs (and the protocols). No laboratory values or electrocardiograms are shown in this lecture.
